name: Variables
reason: Plain names read as text: upstream's own text color is its workbench foreground, which its "Colors" rule also uses.

name: Invalid
reason: Invalid code is an error: upstream's own error red is gitDecoration.deletedResourceForeground.

name: Inserted
reason: Inserted lines are additions: upstream's own color for new files is gitDecoration.untrackedResourceForeground.

name: Deleted
reason: Deleted lines are removals: upstream's own color for deleted files is gitDecoration.deletedResourceForeground.

name: Changed
reason: Changed lines take upstream's own violet, the keyword color, the hue nearest the Material purple.

name: Regular expressions
reason: Regular expressions take upstream's own cyan, editorLineNumber.activeForeground, so they stand apart from the sky blue strings.

name: Escape characters
reason: Escapes read as part of a string pattern, so they take the same cyan as regular expressions.

name: JSON keys
reason: The top-level key color takes upstream's own violet, the hue nearest the Material purple. Orca reads no nested-key selectors, so this is the only key level that ships.

name: Markdown text
reason: Markdown prose reads as text: upstream's own text color is its workbench foreground.

name: Heading marks
reason: The # marks take the mint that upstream's own entity.name rule gives the heading text.

name: Inline code
reason: Inline code takes upstream's own violet, the hue nearest the Material purple.

name: Inline code punctuation
reason: Quiet Markdown syntax marks take upstream's own comment color.

name: Italic
reason: Emphasis takes upstream's own pink, the tag color, the hue nearest the Material red.

name: Bold
reason: Strong emphasis takes the same pink as italic, as upstream gives both one color.

name: Underline
reason: Underline is emphasis, so it takes the same pink as italic and bold.

name: Link titles
reason: Upstream's own String Link rule colors string.other.link mint. A later Material rule overrode the Markdown link.

name: Link descriptions
reason: Link text takes the same link color as link titles.

name: Link references
reason: A link reference is a constant: upstream's own constant color is the yellow of its numbers.

name: Code blocks
reason: Code blocks take the same violet as inline code.

name: Separators
reason: Quiet Markdown syntax marks take upstream's own comment color.

name: Tables
reason: Table text reads as text: upstream's own text color is its workbench foreground.

name: Decorators
reason: Upstream sets none, so Orca would show Dark+. VS Code grammars scope annotations as storage.type.annotation, which upstream's keyword rule colors violet.

name: Constants
reason: Upstream sets none, so Orca would show Dark+. Upstream colors its named constants (constant.language, support.constant) with its number yellow.

name: Log info
reason: Info takes upstream's own info blue, inputValidation.infoBorder and the modified-file color.

name: Log warnings
reason: Warnings take upstream's own warning orange, inputValidation.warningBorder.

name: Log errors
reason: Errors take upstream's own error red, gitDecoration.deletedResourceForeground.

name: Log debug
reason: Debug takes upstream's own violet, the hue nearest the Dark+ purple.

name: --sidebar-foreground
reason: Lightness alone reaches its floors only outside the sRGB gamut (#b08bff to #be9aff, a hue shift), so it takes the nearest comment role, comment, lifted in lightness to #a5a7f9.

name: --text-link
reason: Lightness alone reaches its floors only outside the sRGB gamut (#0084ff to #33a0ff, a hue shift), so it takes the neighboring info role, gitDecoration.modifiedResourceForeground.

name: --diff-removed
reason: Lightness alone reaches its floors only outside the sRGB gamut (#ff004c to #ff4f70, a hue shift), so it takes the neighboring tag role, entity.name.tag.

name: black
reason: Upstream sets no ANSI colors, so VS Code shows its own. This slot takes a dark color in the style's own hue (tab.inactiveBackground).

name: red
reason: Upstream sets no ANSI colors, so VS Code shows its own. This slot takes upstream's error red (gitDecoration.deletedResourceForeground).

name: green
reason: Upstream sets no ANSI colors, so VS Code shows its own. This slot takes upstream's peek view green (peekView.border).

name: yellow
reason: Upstream sets no ANSI colors, so VS Code shows its own. This slot takes upstream's warning orange, so it stays apart from bright yellow (inputValidation.warningBorder).

name: cyan
reason: Upstream sets no ANSI colors, so VS Code shows its own. It would take upstream's cyan, editorLineNumber.activeForeground, 0.000 from the terminal foreground #00ffc8, under 0.06, so it takes the info role (gitDecoration.modifiedResourceForeground), 9.29:1 on the terminal background.

name: blue
reason: Upstream sets no ANSI colors, so VS Code shows its own. It would take upstream's function blue, 0.053 from cyan #00c3ff, under 0.06, so it takes the editorLink role (editorLink.activeForeground), 5.23:1 on the terminal background.

name: magenta
reason: Upstream sets no ANSI colors, so VS Code shows its own. This slot takes upstream's keyword violet (keyword).

name: white
reason: Upstream sets no ANSI colors, so VS Code shows its own. This slot takes upstream's lavender white, its block variable color (meta.block variable.other).

reason: Upstream sets no ANSI colors, so VS Code shows its own. This slot takes upstream's comment color (comment).

name: brightRed
reason: Upstream sets no ANSI colors, so VS Code shows its own. This slot takes upstream's tag pink (entity.name.tag).

name: brightGreen
reason: Upstream sets no ANSI colors, so VS Code shows its own. It would take upstream's mint, its type color, 0.057 from the terminal foreground #00ffc8, under 0.06, so it takes the lime role (terminalCursor.foreground), 15.16:1 on the terminal background.

name: brightYellow

name: brightBlue
reason: Upstream sets no ANSI colors, so VS Code shows its own. It would take upstream's sky blue, its string color, 0.055 from cyan #00c3ff, under 0.06, so it takes the method role (entity.name.method.js), 6.56:1 on the terminal background.

name: brightMagenta

name: brightCyan
reason: Upstream sets no ANSI colors, so VS Code shows its own. This slot takes upstream's pale cyan, its CSS property color (source.css support.type.property-name).

name: brightWhite
reason: Upstream sets no ANSI colors, so VS Code shows its own. This slot takes upstream's white, its workbench foreground (foreground).
